why: The owner asked (Nov 1): 'why is nanomuse the reviewer, what is this', and for a 'Models used' page that explains how we use each model, emphasizes Meta's models, and marks fallbacks to other models with *. Every fact below comes from a run record or the owner's rules, listed under sources.

page.title: Models used
linked_from: Agora header nav: The film · How it works · Use cases · Models used · Decks · Evidence
Eranos request page, calm view, after 'One helper at a time. Every step is recorded.': 'Which model does what ↗'
page.render_from: This file. No number on the page may be typed by hand.

rules: Meta first: every step defaults to a Muse model through the Meta API, at the standard tier (owner, Nov 1).
Name models, not agent apps. An agent app (Muse Code, nanoMuse, OpenClaw...) is not a model. Agent apps appear only in the 'Volunteers' AIs' table on this page.
A * marks a model that is not Meta's: a fallback, or a model used only in tests.
If a fallback ever answers, the request page names it next to the step it did.
No receipts, hashes or run ids on the page. Dates, durations, counts and versions only.

steps.text: No model. The request waits in a durable queue.
Muse Spark 1.3 splits it into Tasks.

steps.agent_app: Muse Code, when the work needs code
steps.text_design: Muse Spark 1.3, in Muse Code when it needs code.
steps.why_changed: The dedicated workers call Muse Spark 1.3 directly; Muse Code ran the build only in the Oct 31 test run.

steps.text: No model. The check waits for a second agent.
Muse Spark 1.3, a second agent with its own key.
No model. A person at the nonprofit decides.

meta_models.name: Muse Spark 1.3
meta_models.role: Splits a request into Tasks, does the work and checks another agent's work. Our dedicated workers use it.

tested.text: Test run: one agent built a kit with it in 3 min 27 s (207.27 s, 25 model calls); a second agent with its own key checked it in 1 min 23 s (82.73 s, 14 model calls).
It finished the full claim · do · report test in three agent apps: Muse Code, nanoMuse and OpenClaw.

meta_models.variant_note: The Oct 31 test run used muse-spark-1.3-contributor, which we use only for public test work. Live requests use the standard tier; Herma refuses Contributor variants for real requests.

meta_models.name: Muse Code 1.4.14
meta_models.kind: agent app by Meta (not a model)
meta_models.role: Runs Muse Spark 1.3 when a request needs code: it writes the files, runs the tests and reports back to the queue.

tested.text: Built the weekly shift-schedule kit, with 8 tests and a README, in 25 model calls.

meta_models.name: Muse Wonder 1.0
meta_models.role: Writes test scenarios and typed proposals, one at a time. Each one is checked against its schema and never runs by itself.

tested.text: Our scenario generator runs it, with a self-test.

meta_models.name: Muse Glimmer 30B
meta_models.role: Fills in Task Object forms and tool calls exactly, so a worker's report fits the queue the first time.

tested.text: Exact tool-call match rose from 93.3% to 99.3% on our 150-case test, tuned and measured on Kaggle on two T4 GPUs.

meta_models.serving_note: Measured, not serving requests. Do not claim it answers live requests.
meta_models.note: Tuned and tested by ta-amps; the live workers run Muse Spark 1.3 through the Meta API.

film_models.name: SAM
film_models.role: Finds the parts of the page in each frame, so captions stay clear of them.
film_models.tested: Overlap between captions and page parts fell from 0.281 to 0.037.
film_models.why_state: Measured on the earlier v6 film; becomes measured again when the same check runs on the new cut.

film_models.name: wav2vec 2.0
film_models.role: Times each caption to the narration.
film_models.tested: Checks every caption against what is said.
film_models.why_state: Measured on the earlier v6 film; becomes measured again when the same check runs on the new cut.

film_models.name: MusicGen
film_models.role: Wrote the film's music, so there is no licensed track.
film_models.tested: One original underscore, made on our computer.

nanomuse.what: A small open-source agent app (v1.0.8), not a model and not made by Meta. Public listings describe it as an open-source personal agent from a Zhejiang University team.
nanomuse.why_it_was_the_checker: The Oct 31 test run used two different agent apps and two different keys, so the checker could never be the builder: Muse Code built, nanoMuse checked, and both ran Muse Spark 1.3.
nanomuse.page_copy: An open-source agent app, not a model and not made by Meta. In our Oct 31 test run it was the second agent: it ran Muse Spark 1.3 with its own key and checked the kit another agent built (8 tests passed, 0 rule violations).
nanomuse.owner_decision: Keep nanoMuse as one tested agent app, or run the dedicated checker in Muse Code under a second key so every app named in the film is Meta's. The page is correct either way.

fallbacks.name: Claude Haiku 4.5 *
fallbacks.role: A fallback Herma can call with the project's own key.

fallbacks.name: GPT-4.1 nano *
fallbacks.role: A second fallback Herma can call with the project's own key.

other_non_meta.name: Kimi K2.7 Code *
other_non_meta.use: Only as the model in three agent-app tests on Oct 29 (Hermes, OpenCode, Pi).

other_non_meta.name: Kokoro 82M *
other_non_meta.use: The film's narration voice. The Meta API offers transcription but no speaking voice.

featured_use_case.title: A food pantry's weekly shift schedule
featured_use_case.label: Recorded test run · Oct 31
featured_use_case.asked: Each week our volunteers tell us when they can come in. Please build us a small kit that turns our volunteer availability CSV into a weekly shift schedule that meets our coverage rules, with tests and a README, so our own agent or staff can run it.
rules: 12 shifts, Monday to Saturday, morning and afternoon
only shifts a volunteer is available for
nobody on both shifts of one day

steps.title: Split into two Tasks
steps.text: Build the kit; check the kit.

steps.title: Waiting for a person
steps.text: Nothing is used or published until someone at the pantry says yes.
